title: Latency fingerprint runbook + trace-hook integrator for adaptive alert thresholds
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight integration that extracts per-route latency fingerprints, wires them into our runbook automation, and uses trace-hooks to correlate anomalies with upstream context so burn-rate and paging thresholds can auto-adjust.

Context: Current burn-rate alerts are static across many routes and overly sensitive during short, non-actionable spikes (e.g., slow cold-start VMs, probe storms). We need a system that learns baseline latency shapes (p50/p90/p99 waveform across request lifetime), attaches a stable fingerprint to a route, and enables a runbook-driven policy to suppress noisy pages while keeping SLO fidelity.

This ticket covers: (1) a small trace-hook shim that annotates spans with route fingerprint metadata and sampling-decisions; (2) an enrichment pipeline that merges those annotations into metric rollups; (3) a runbook mapping UI definition (Console) to declare silent-window and escalation tweaks for matched fingerprints; (4) alert rule transformer that proposes adjusted burn-rate thresholds and suppression windows for review by oncall owners.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-hook shim deployed as sidecar or agent that adds 'latency_fingerprint' and 'fingerprint_version' tags to sampled spans on target services
Enrichment pipeline emits route-level fingerprint metrics into the observability cluster with <= 15s propagation
Console runbook UI exposes fingerprint -> suppression mapping and preview simulation for a 72-hour historical window
Alert transformer can generate a draft burn-rate rule with recommended suppression window and confidence score; drafts require manual approval before auto-apply
End-to-end test: synthetic slow-tail spike on staging produces a draft rule that reduces pages by >= 60% for same SLO signal without missing genuine regressions in 5 simulated incidents
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Evaluated two fingerprinting algorithms (histogram sketch vs. quantile-derivative). Decided to start with a quantile-derivative pipeline (smaller memory, deterministic) and keep histogram sketch as follow-up.

2026-02-20: Prototype trace-hook implemented (Go/OTel). Minimal changes to instrumentation: adds 'lat_fp_v1' tag computed from p50/p95 slope across last 20 requests. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-agent/pull/256

2026-02-28: Ingestion team validated metric schemas. Added new metric series: observability.route_latency_fingerprint and observability.fingerprint_confidence. Draft schema stored in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Latency+Fingerprint+Schema

2026-03-04: UX critique with Console PM and Design. Designer suggested adding a 'preview simulation' that shows historical page counts if rule were applied. Design mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcPreviewMock

2026-03-08: Integration test failed in staging: sampling rate too low for low-traffic routes -> insufficient confidence. Action: add adaptive sampling policy (min 1 event per minute per route) and backfill using tail-based sampling heuristics.
risks: Over-suppression: incorrect fingerprint matching could silence real incidents — mitigating by requiring manual approval for first 30 days and confidence threshold >= 0.75
Cost: additional cardinality in metrics ingestion; mitigate by compressing fingerprint namespace (bucketization) and TTL for low-usage fingerprints
Instrumentation drift: services with custom tracing setups may not tag spans consistently. Plan: a small compatibility shim and telemetry QA checklist for services to opt-in
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for fingerprint computation and deterministic versioning. 2) End-to-end staging test that injects synthetic latency shapes via chaos runner (link to job). 3) Canary rollout with 10% of services for 48h, monitor false-positive rate and paging counts. 4) Post-mortem runbook to revert auto-adjust rules if missed regressions detected.
